transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Um, hi. I guess... I'm just having a hard time keeping things organized lately. I have my schoolwork, and I have this little accessories shop I do, and I just can't seem to manage both at the same time. Like, all my supplies, receipts, due dates, assignment notes... they just end up in these piles everywhere. And then I just... I don't really know what to do first. So, yeah. That's why I came in.
Have you always struggled with staying organized and managing tasks, even back in childhood or earlier school years, or is this something that started more recently?

I guess... yeah, it's always been like this. Um, my mom actually still has some of my old notes from teachers back in elementary school. They usually complained that I was always getting out of my seat... or talking before they called on me. And that I'd just rush through group activities, even when I already understood the work. So... it's not really a new thing.
Right now, as an adult, do you still notice things like feeling restless, having trouble sitting still, or blurting things out or acting impulsively, in addition to the disorganization?

I guess so, yeah. Um... I don't know, even when I'm not really doing anything or going anywhere, I just... I feel this sort of buzzing inside. Like my body just needs to move. It's... it's worse when I'm supposed to just sit there and listen to someone.
Do you notice these struggles with organization, restlessness, and impulsivity happening in multiple areas of your life—like both at home and at work or school—or is it mostly limited to one setting?

Um... I'm not really sure. I guess it's just... everywhere. Like I said before, it happens with my school stuff, and with the shop at home. I haven't really thought about it being limited to just one place.
